open_risks.text: Write the threat model BEFORE any gate code — the whole point of this thread is that six rounds escalated because the assurance level was never written down, and code first would repeat it

The gate fails OPEN on its own bugs — only exit code 2 blocks, so a crash, a timeout or malformed output all let the command run; c3 exists because this is the highest-leverage fix available and it is a few lines

The G5 parser still has a differential space — a python3 -c invocation using a built-in HTTP client evades a named-command list, so unrecognized-but-file-reference-shaped input must fail to ask, never to allow
Five controls means five drift surfaces where the monolith had one — this is the strongest argument against the decomposition and it was accepted knowingly; treat the shape as revisable, not settled

Token scoping cannot prevent merge — GitHub gates the merge endpoint on the Contents permission, which the agent needs anyway to push branches; server-side branch protection is the only real control for G1
Never delete branch archive/gate-parser-rewrite-2026-08-05 — commit 21ae349 is the only copy of the rewrite and holds the INV-4 structural fix and expanded tests worth mining for this rebuild

Changing .claude/settings.json is the user's call — the sandbox credential deny that would close G5 at OS level is available and cheap, but settings drift belongs to the permission-config-audit thread

key_decisions.title: The bash gate is a defense-in-depth control at a scoped assurance level, not a security boundary
Abandon general bash parsing; decompose the five protections into five per-action controls
Archive the rejected rewrite and restore HEAD's regex gate as the live guard

out_of_scope: Making the gate withstand a determined human attacker - that person is the machine owner with unrestricted shell access outside Claude Code already, so no hook raises their effective privilege bar
Perfect bash parsing fidelity - the acceptance bar is that uncertainty degrades to ask, never to a silent allow
